gen-fs-pencerio-nunito-sans: Formal ink, tightly knit. Pencerio brings a calligraphic hand that earns its place big and brief, while Nunito Sans stays soft beside it, curves wide open.
gen-fs-quilon-noto-serif: Noto Serif reads literary and a touch prominent, its strokes swelling and thinning gently. Quilon, a display face, does its best work shouting editorial with tall open shapes, while the classic serif settles into quieter, bookish phrasing.
gen-fs-rosaline-dm-sans: DM Sans reads friendly and approachable, its s terminals spread wide and welcoming. And Rosaline, all flowing pen strokes with stems far heavier than its crossbars, sits closed and luxurious above it, so scale the sans up a touch.
gen-fs-rosaline-newsreader: Sharp edges against fat darkness, written by hand. Newsreader answers with open, refined curves and a restrained stem, so Rosaline's closed letters get room to breathe.
gen-fs-telma-bitter: Telma writes in flowing pen strokes, its lowercase a wide-mouthed and its mean line held high. And Bitter, a slab-serif with a big, grounded lowercase, gives those loops something dependable to stand on.
gen-fs-telma-instrument-sans: Graceful loops, then clean lines. Telma's pen-written letters keep a mild stress that stays solid, while Instrument Sans follows with a sans-serif stroke that never shifts weight on any curve.
gen-fs-telma-inter: Understated handwriting meets tidy modern type, with Telma's stems only slightly outweighing its hairlines. Inter's breathing counters feel smooth and level beside it.
gen-fs-telma-mulish: Graceful describes Telma's flowing pen letters, with horizontals lighter but never threadlike, set against Mulish, whose strokes never swell or thin. That contrast of handwriting and cable-bent sans is the pair's whole charm.
gen-fs-telma-roboto-slab: Understated, Telma writes with a restrained thick-thin rhythm and a high mean line. Roboto Slab brings structure, a slab-serif whose open throats and dense middle zone feel precise.
gen-gf-aboreto-fs-paquito: Aboreto sprawls wide, with open bowls and brush-pressed stems. Should it shrink small, those hairline connectors fade, and Paquito's confident classic serif would crowd out the heading.
